questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose Monash University, Melbourne, Australia, since I preferred a country where the first language was English. Furthermore Monash is Australias biggest university and they have a great reputation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, both UCHP and Monash provided a lot of information. Additionally I knew a few people who had been on exchange in Australia and Melbourne, who could also help me with my questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Study Abord team was really great in helping with changing units and schedule problems. Also, one of my professors was really nice and helped me out with some unit correlations and advise.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Everything about the study and the formal part worked well, e.g, changing units and so on. However the the social part of the orientation was mediocre. The events were not that great and there weren't that many.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at a place called Yugo (they have multiple sites worldwide), which a friend recommended to me. I booked before I arrived in Melbourne.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great! I only had classes 2-3 times a week and the campus was 1 hour out of the site. The campus is located in a very quiet area, and it is quite difficult getting from campus and into the centrum in the evenings. All of my friends lived off campus as well, so we always hung out other places than campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember much besides that there was a formula that you needed to fill out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mostly got help from other students who were going to the same university as I was

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: All went fine

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 3/4 units were really great and I learned a lot. The last one wasn't that great organized.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the units were appropriate. Some were a bit easier and a some were a bit more challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were no lectures, we only had workshops (klassetimer in danish). We had some lectures which were recorded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BMS5001 - Research Training: Critical Thinking and Communication Skills 
BMS5005 - Regenerative Medicine and Stem Cells
BMS5007 - Biotechnology: Commercialising biomedical science
MGF5928 - Strategic Leadership

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BMS5001, BMS5007 and MGF5928
They were all greatly organized. 
I learned a lot in BMS5001 - the professor is great. 
BMS5007: it was an easier unit since some of the materials were already covered by UCHP, however, they added the aspect of investment and marketing. 
MGF5928: great introduction course to leadership. It was more focused on the top management of a company (such as CEO and so on), however we learned some great tools to analyse a business and understand the perspective of the top management.

The flight tickets were more expensive than what I expected (the price had increased a lot after covid)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The flight tickets

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The are not that many clubs or sports clubs you can join. - I also lived off campus and I wasn't at campus every day which made it more difficult for me to join a club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't remember

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None since I did not attend any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The winter/spring in Melbourne can be cold and wet, so I would go to the north in the mid-semester break in October. I went to Cairns, Cape Tribulation and Whitsundays which was great.
I went to Sydney over a weekend (5 days) during the semester. I went to Tasmania (9 days) and Western Australia (3,5 weeks) after my semester. I loved all of it!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, it came quite natural

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australia is very western and laid back. Everyone is very open, sweet, and helpful. The Australian people an absolutely lovely.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find accommodation off campus. It is not worth living close to campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I got.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is very different from Denmark. There are a lot of assignments during the semester, which I was not used to and I therefore spent a lot of time during school work during some evenings.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
